name: Pizza Funghi
steps: Combine flour, yeast, 300 ml lukewarm water and 25 ml olive oil. Add 8 g salt and the remaining 25 ml water; knead for 8–10 minutes until elastic. Put in a lightly oiled bowl, cover and let rise in a warm place for roughly 90 minutes until doubled.

Wipe the mushrooms clean and slice them 4–5 mm thick. Heat 10 ml olive oil in a broad pan over medium-high heat. Spread the mushrooms in a single layer and cook for 5–6 minutes, stirring only after they start to brown, until their released moisture evaporates. Add finely chopped garlic and the remaining 1 g salt for the final 30 seconds; cool on a plate.

Drain the mozzarella thoroughly and blot it dry. Mix the passata with oregano and 2 g salt. Heat the oven to 250°C, or its hottest safe pizza setting, with a heavy tray or stone inside for at least 25 minutes. Divide the risen dough into two equal portions and stretch each on lightly floured baking paper into a 28-cm round.

Spread half the seasoned tomato on the first base, leaving a 2-cm rim. Add half the mozzarella and half the browned mushrooms, spreading them evenly rather than piling them in the centre. Drizzle with 5 ml olive oil and a little black pepper.

Slide the pizza with its paper onto the hot tray and bake for 10–14 minutes until the base is cooked, the rim is deeply golden and the cheese bubbles. Assemble and bake the second pizza with the remaining sauce, cheese, mushrooms, 5 ml oil and black pepper.

Scatter fresh basil over both pizzas after baking and cut each into four slices. Serve two slices per person. The mushroom pieces should remain visible and browned, and the pizza base should be crisp rather than wet.
tips: Browning mushrooms first removes moisture that would otherwise soak the pizza. Use mozzarella made with microbial or vegetable rennet. Keep basil for after baking so it stays green and fresh.
notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.
